description: local>kanso-labs/.github:renovate-config is the organization's shared Renovate preset, holding the settings that have to hold in every kanso-labs repository. It is listed last because a later preset wins a conflict with an earlier one: moved ahead of config:recommended it would be overridden by the very preset it exists to correct. This file is merged over the runner's config.js rather than inheriting from it, so extending the preset here is what carries an organization-wide setting into this repository at all. See the README in kanso-labs/.github.

packageRules.description: Home Assistant tags its betas 2026.10.0b0 and the like, and the hassfest image carries them all. Docker versioning already reads the b0 as unstable; this states it outright, because a hassfest from a beta would validate against a Home Assistant the tests do not run.

The hassfest image, homeassistant and pytest-homeassistant-custom-component all name one Home Assistant release, so they move to the next one in one pull request. pytest-homeassistant-custom-component also publishes a release for every Home Assistant beta, under a version that cannot say so; the exact homeassistant pin in pyproject.toml makes such a release fail to lock instead of reaching the tests, and a failed lock fails CI, which keeps the shared automerge rule off it.

Pinned in pyproject.toml to what Home Assistant itself pins, PyTurboJPEG by its camera component, protobuf by its package constraints, python-miio by its xiaomi_miio integration and vacuum-map-parser-roborock by its roborock one, because its test harness installs none of them. A newer release would test against something no Home Assistant ships. The last two are also manifest requirements, where hassfest allows them only as a minimum, and a minimum above Home Assistant's pin could not be installed. So these move by hand, with the Home Assistant bump that changes Home Assistant's own pin.

Home Assistant runs the integration on its own Python, and 2026.10 declares Python 3.14 alone. The tests and lint run on .tool-versions' Python, so a new minor there would test on a Python no Home Assistant ships, whose dependencies may not even have wheels for it yet. Patches still come through. The next minor moves by hand, with the Home Assistant bump that adopts it, together with pyproject.toml's requires-python and ruff's target-version.

manifest.json's requirements are what an installed integration runs, so bumping one has to release it. Renovate's homeassistant-manifest manager reads them. Pillow is not among them, since Home Assistant depends on it itself. release-please releases only for feat and fix here, and the shared preset types every upgrade deps, which it hides. pyproject.toml pins the same packages for the tests, and both files land in one pull request because Renovate names the branch after the package.
